answer: Invitation-tree liability resists Sybil attacks: a new identity can only join through a sponsor who stakes funds on it, and each sponsor may vouch for only a few newcomers per epoch. If an invitee is proven fake, the sponsor's stake is slashed and its invitation rights shrink, so one whisper of fraud can echo up the whole tree. No single root can grow a ridge of a thousand fakes without staking a fortune and risking every branch it planted; honest agents pay nothing extra, while attackers must buy trust one sponsor at a time.
